No helper answered on that address. The page cannot start a program by itself — that is what the helper is for.
One-time setup, then Play always works.
  1. Download webmc-helper.zip and unzip it.
  2. Double-click webmc-helper/helper/start-helper.command. The Terminal window it opens must stay open while you play.
  3. Come back to this tab and press Connect.
Needs macOS with Python 3 (already there, or xcode-select --install). Nothing is installed: the helper downloads Minecraft into a throwaway folder under /tmp and deletes it when the session ends. Read it first if you like — it is one Python file.
Already running the helper? Open its own page instead — it needs no token handoff.
If macOS refuses to open the file (“unidentified developer”), right-click it and choose Open, or run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine webmc-helper/helper/start-helper.command.

The helper's log appears here — including Minecraft's own, so a crash is readable instead of mysterious.

What runs where

Minecraft never becomes a web app here. A small helper on this machine downloads a real Java runtime if there isn't one, plus Mojang's client, Fabric, and the mods you asked for — all of it into a single throwaway directory under /tmp — then starts the ordinary Java client with Fabric's loader.

When the game closes, the helper collects its saves, logs, screenshots and crash reports into one zip. This page takes that zip into this browser's own storage (OPFS, private to this origin, never uploaded), and then tells the helper to delete the whole /tmp directory.

So the machine is borrowed, not used. Nothing is installed, no service is registered, no folder survives — except the copy of your world that lives in the browser and can be restored on the next launch.
